implicated work-descriptions.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) is responsible for investigating client requirements for statistical information, defining project objectives and priorities, and determining sources of data for special requests (e.g., 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used.'). This includes modifying existing techniques or developing new approaches to meet specific needs, integrating data from various sources, and providing expert advice to users inside and outside the organization. Future GSBPM expectation: The future state of 'Identify needs' demands that staff proactively scan all existing data holdings and alternative data sources first, and employ rigorous cost-benefit, timeliness, and risk assessments before initiating any new data collections or surveys. There is an explicit expectation for solution-oriented thinking, automation, reuse, and documentation to support digital workflows, with new data collection being a last resort, justified only as necessary. Role evolution: The EC-05 role will need to evolve from responding to client needs with a survey-first or special study mindset, toward leading a thorough digital/data asset discovery, leveraging internal and external data, and systematically validating if a new collection is required. Decision-making will become more evidence-based, documented, and digitally traceable, with a requirement to challenge default assumptions and construct robust business cases for new surveys. Earlier and more formalized stakeholder engagement will include feasibility, automation, and AI considerations. Capability implication: Greater importance will be placed on in-depth knowledge of data sources (internal, administrative, external), digital navigation skills for metadata-assisted data discovery, the ability to conduct and document cost-benefit-risk analyses, an understanding of automation and AI readiness, and the capability to communicate and justify complex, resource-driven decisions to both clients and internal governance.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) plans and implements long-term program strategies, develops policies, assesses program requirements, and reviews the conceptual framework for statistical programs (e.g., 'Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.'). The position is responsible for determining data acquisition methods, assessing trends, and integrating data from various sources, often including data not originally collected for current purposes. Future GSBPM expectation: The revised 'Identify needs' phase now serves as a strategic enterprise-wide gatekeeper, with a proactive obligation to scan all data assets for reusability, assess operational feasibility of new collections, and apply dynamic cost/timeliness/risk trade-offs. This function is essential to realizing StatCan2030’s objectives for efficiency, digital enablement, and resource optimization. Role evolution: This leadership role will shift toward enforcing digital-first, cross-program data asset utilization and implementing standardized needs identification procedures supported by digital platforms (e.g., data inventories, risk/cost tracking tools). EC-06 incumbents must drive this culture change and ensure that proposals for new projects include thorough, auditable documentation of needs assessment, alternative data explorations, and automation-readiness. They will increasingly participate in resource trade-off decisions, digital workflow alignment, and must build and reinforce mechanisms for early, digitally-enabled stakeholder engagement. Capability implication: This elevates the importance of strategic data asset management expertise, awareness of digital and AI technologies for discovery and automation, advanced understanding of cost/risk frameworks, and the ability to champion cross-organizational change toward digital, sustainable statistical production.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Head, Production and Dissemination

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' (EC-04) develops and implements statistical processing systems, designs data specifications, and conducts feasibility studies for new systems and projects, often collaborating across divisions (e.g., 'Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program.'). The role also negotiates procedural modifications, provides guidance on subject-matter requirements, and analyzes current methods for relevancy and improvement. Future GSBPM expectation: Needs identification must now precede all project proposals with structured digital scanning for existing data and explicit operational feasibility analyses, considering digital, AI, and automation capabilities from the outset. System enhancements or new data collections must be justified by documented inability to fulfill requirements with existing assets. Role evolution: The officer's work will move from mainly evaluating the technical fit of new requirements in the context of system development, to actively engaging in a standardized, enterprise-driven needs identification funnel. This means greater responsibility for conducting and documenting data asset and system audits, collaborating with business intelligence tools for rapid discovery, and steering feasibility assessments that incorporate automation, digital workflow compatibility, and sustainability perspectives. Capability implication: Increasingly critical are capabilities in digital inventory navigation, understanding of metadata standards and federated data sourcing, and operationalizing cost-benefit-risk analysis at the systems and process design stage, as well as synthesizing this information for formal project decision points.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator' (EC-03) coordinates data retrieval, validation, and dissemination; recommends and implements changes to improve statistical systems and processes; and acts as a subject-matter liaison for user requirements (e.g., 'Identifies and assesses trends and developments in the subject area; reviews the potential impact on program subject-matter content and determines the implications for statistical methods and procedures.'). The role involves interpreting user requests, identifying sources of information, and analyzing and recommending modifications to current data collection and processing approaches. Future GSBPM expectation: With needs identification becoming an upfront, digital-first, and cross-program responsibility, the coordinator is expected to perform proactive scans for data reuse, contribute to cost and timeliness analyses, and rigorously document the rationale for new collections. Engagement with clients and data users becomes more structured and evidence-based, relying on digital tools to assess the feasibility and sustainability of meeting statistical needs. Role evolution: EC-03 incumbents will transition from a largely responsive approach to user requests, to a proactive gatekeeping and diagnostic role, systematically leveraging agency data assets, automation capabilities, and digital discovery tools before escalating requests to new projects. They will need to integrate operational feasibility and digital readiness assessments into their workflow, and record rationales in standardized formats supporting automation and audit. Capability implication: Emphasized will be knowledge of digital data inventories, metadata-driven search and evaluation, process documentation for audit and design handover, and the ability to synthesize and communicate operational constraints and readiness for automation to both internal stakeholders and clients.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator
Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is responsible for investigating client requirements for statistical information, defining the nature and scope of special studies, and determining sources of data for special requests and studies. As per the work description, they 'provide subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC' and 'knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on program results.' These responsibilities inherently include the consultation and confirmation of stakeholder needs and translating these into statistical products.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future-state for consulting and confirming needs shifts from a focus on initiating new data collection to a model in which existing and alternative data holdings are examined first, leveraging AI-supported platforms and automated discovery tools. Consultations will be more rapid, iterative, outcome-driven, and will emphasize transparent assessment of trade-offs, value, and reusability, with new survey launches being a last resort following explicit, documented justification and cost-benefit analysis.

Role evolution: The EC-05 role will shift from lengthy, exploratory consultations toward facilitating joint assessments of user needs via digital platforms that highlight available holdings and trade-offs. Rather than defaulting to proposing special studies and custom surveys, the specialist will guide stakeholders through the possibilities and limitations of what can be delivered from current assets, using shared metadata and automated tools to evaluate feasibility, timeliness, and value. The role will also require structured documentation and explanation of decision pathways, rationale for rejecting new survey initiation, and negotiation based on the organization’s prioritization criteria. Interactions with clients will be more frequent, agile, and will require real-time, data-driven dialogue.

Capability implication: The new emphasis on data discovery and automated consultation platforms demands much deeper knowledge of agency data holdings, advanced facility with digital data discovery and metadata tools, and fluency in facilitating transparent discussions around data quality, fitness-for-use, value trade-offs, and cost-benefit within fast-paced, outcome-focused cycles. A greater understanding of automated decision support systems, AI-augmented discovery tools, and the rationale for prioritization based on organizational strategy will become vital for effective performance in the redefined consultation process.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Head, Production and Dissemination
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination, plans and implements strategies for statistical programs, prepares program proposals, develops policies and guidelines, and provides expert advisory and consultative services to users. The position involves 'investigating client requirements for statistical information and determining the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements,' and requires knowledge of key client department policies to identify and respond to information needs. The current approach supports both custom development and adaption of existing methods/products in response to evolving client demand, often in a consultative, iterative fashion.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future-state, program launch and needs confirmation become highly evidence-driven, prioritizing reuse, automation, and cost efficiency. Strategy and program decisions will require explicit resource alignment and justification for any new data collection, with consultations underpinned by shared, transparent platforms tracking needs, commitments, and trade-off decisions. The role expands into stewardship of the consultation ecosystem: ensuring staff leverage digital tools, that process cycles are short and trackable, and that agency prioritization (what gets built) is transparent and defensible. Decision-logging and metadata-driven alignment are integral parts of this expectation.

Role evolution: The Head’s responsibilities will move toward embedding real-time consultation support mechanisms, monitoring and guiding the adoption of digital platforms for needs consultation, and defining the boundary conditions for when new collections are justified. Leadership will shift away from supporting exploratory program expansions to enforcing a rigorous structure of reuse-first, feasibility-driven, and transparently documented consultations. Accountability will include tracking consultation timelines, overseeing trade-off and cost-benefit deliberations, and ensuring continuous process improvement through feedback loops captured in shared tools.

Capability implication: This creates a heightened need for expertise in digital product/platform development for stakeholder consultation, oversight of automated and AI-augmented consultation workflows, advanced resource optimization, and knowledge of performance analytics for process cycles (timeliness, reuse rates, rejection/acceptance of new data collection proposals). Deep understanding of policy, strategic prioritization, and the mechanisms for effective, transparent trade-off discussions will be necessary, as well as change management proficiency to shepherd the workforce through these operational and cultural shifts.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator coordinates the retrieval, validation, and dissemination of data, provides custom tabulations for ad-hoc client requests, and 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' Other key duties include interpreting user requests, determining feasibility, and advising on subject-matter concepts, which places them on the front line of traditional stakeholder needs consultation.

Future GSBPM expectation: The modernization agenda transforms this liaison and translation function into an evidence-based, digital consultation workflow, requiring the Coordinator to use machine-actionable metadata platforms to rapidly determine if client needs can be met from assets already available. Further, only when needs clearly cannot be met via current holdings—and following cost-benefit driven, transparent discussions—will new tabulation or data collection proposals advance. Cycles are shortened, and emphasis is placed on maximizing reusability, minimizing burden, and documenting all decision processes.

Role evolution: The Coordinator’s process will need to rely far less on iterative, person-to-person exploratory investigation and more on expert navigation of metadata/discovery platforms, facilitating rapid, value-driven assessments in collaboration with clients. This includes helping stakeholders navigate automated results, surfacing trade-offs transparently, and ensuring that every need assessment is documented and aligned with agency priority and asset availability. The role will also have to respond to and participate in more frequent process feedback and realignment cycles.

Capability implication: This evolution privileges deep operational familiarity with agency metadata, data discovery and exploration platforms, knowledge of how to audit and surface reusability and feasibility of data, and agility in leading clients through digital consultation cycles. The role also grows to require fluency in articulating resource, respondent burden, and value trade-offs in language accessible to non-technical users, as well as proficiency in logging and tracking these decisions for management review.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist plays a critical role in defining project objectives and priorities, preparing work plans outlining approaches, timeframes, and resources, and determining sources of data for special requests or studies. This includes deciding whether to use existing data sources or to initiate new collection efforts (see: 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used.'). The Specialist also interprets user needs, integrates data from various sources, and negotiates with system specialists, methodologists, and clients regarding resources, timeframes, and costs.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, establishing output objectives will require defaulting to the reuse of existing data holdings and demonstrating the infeasibility of meeting needs through alternative or administrative data before proposing new survey activity. Objectives must also embed automation, machine-readability, and interoperability as standard requirements, with explicit digital execution constraints in place from the outset. Resource discipline and a justification-based approach to any manual or custom methods are now front-loaded in the acceptance of objectives.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will need to shift from responding flexibly to client or user needs with bespoke or survey-based solutions, to proactively justifying all proposed data sources and methods within the context of digital-first, automation-enabled, and resource-efficient workflows. The role's responsibility for defining project objectives will be more tightly intertwined with demonstrating compliance with agency-wide automation, interoperability, and reuse criteria, requiring more structured evidence and documentation, and more direct collaboration with IT and data governance experts upfront. The determination of data sources and methods now involves systematic assessment of digital and operational feasibility, not just subject-matter relevance.

Capability implication: As a result, this role will increasingly depend on deep knowledge of internal data assets and agency data architecture, applied understanding of automation and interoperability requirements for output design, digital evaluation techniques, and the frameworks for cost-benefit analysis as applied to statistical output scoping in a digital context. Evaluating trade-offs among reuse, automation, survey scope, and digital scalability will become essential to this role's effectiveness.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Head, Production and Dissemination
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination is responsible for planning and implementing long-term strategies for statistical programs, developing and recommending frameworks, policies, and guidelines, and preparing program proposals outlining statistical frameworks, strategies, and resource implications ('Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.'). The Head also defines the methods and practices for data acquisition, production, and dissemination, and manages the evaluation of new data sources and systems for their feasibility and program impact.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future-state output objective establishment process is considerably redefined: it mandates that objectives prioritize asset reuse, automation-readiness, digital and resource efficiency, and interoperability by default, with demonstrable justification for any custom/manual or survey-first approaches. Approval for output objectives thus shifts toward an investment-style gate, tightly linked to enterprise architecture, automation pipelines, and digital resource limitations.

Role evolution: The EC-06 will now need to ensure all program and project proposals systematically demonstrate adherence to reuse, automation, and interoperability gates before advancing, integrating enterprise architecture and IT conversations into the earliest scoping and objective-setting decisions. This role will lead in formalizing processes and criteria for objective acceptance, establishing requirements for automation, and enforcing resource and feasibility discipline. It will require more structured collaboration across program, subject-matter, IT, and data governance leads to present business cases for any non-standard output.

Capability implication: The change elevates the importance of strategic data asset stewardship, deep alignment with enterprise IT and automation standards, and the capability to analyze, synthesize, and communicate cost-benefit and digital feasibility arguments at the program acceptance stage. The Head must also be able to balance statistical relevance with digital architecture constraints, and audit or establish processes for evaluating output proposals against agency-wide, automation-first priorities.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer develops processing systems, designs specifications for testing and maintenance, and assesses subject-matter changes and their impact on methods, systems and program results. This includes participation in translating user or program requirements into systems specifications and operational project plans, as well as leading teams in the implementation of new or modified systems ('Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data').

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state necessitates that output objectives, and by extension any supporting system or operational plan, are justified for re-use, automation, and interoperability at inception. The Officer's assessments must now include not just technical feasibility, but digital alignment, resource constraints, and explicit elimination or justification of custom/manual or new data collection methods wherever possible, with digital system integration as a primary criterion.

Role evolution: The EC-04 will need to actively embed automation, interoperability, and reuse principles into all initial assessments, modifications, and systems designs. Their project proposals and system specifications must provide evidence of compliance with digital priorities and resource discipline before advancing, and they will need to negotiate and translate these constraints in interaction with subject-matter and IT stakeholders from the outset. Instead of accommodating user-driven custom solutions by default, they now enforce digital supply chain standards upfront and help develop the rationale for exceptions.

Capability implication: This evolution makes knowledge of agency data holdings, automation frameworks, digital integration constraints, and the rationale for cost/efficiency trade-offs crucial. The role’s analytical focus will shift toward digital system design thinking, interoperability certification, and resource-justification frameworks within output objective-setting, in addition to subject-matter and statistical methodology.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 role currently involves providing subject matter advice on statistical concepts, developing or modifying concepts and definitions, and interpreting user requests to determine data needs. This includes 'develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques', and 'provides advice to data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database.' These activities are typically performed in a manual, expert-driven fashion, based heavily on user requirements and program-specific expertise.

Future GSBPM expectation: The emergence of metadata-driven, AI-assisted tools fundamentally changes the approach to concept identification. The future process places less emphasis on ground-up, ad hoc definition of concepts and instead expects rapid, system-supported discovery, alignment with enterprise standards, and machine-actionable outputs. Human experts are expected to validate, prioritize, and arbitrate rather than generate concepts from scratch.

Role evolution: This role transitions from individually driven, manual curation of concepts and user needs interpretation to orchestrating and overseeing automated concept identification tools. The EC-03 is expected to assess outputs of AI/metadata systems, steer harmonization with enterprise assets, and provide judgment in cases of conceptual alignment, conflict, or gap resolution.

Capability implication: This change increases the importance of understanding enterprise data holdings, metadata standards, AI-based recommendation logic, and the principles of interoperability. The ability to evaluate and arbitrate among system-suggested concepts, ensuring FAIR alignment and program coherence, supersedes the prior focus on manual, bottom-up subject-matter development.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 is accountable for developing subject-matter concepts and definitions, leading system development, and addressing problems in the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of statistical information. Relevant to concept identification, they 'develop subject-matter concepts and definitions', 'propose new statistical methods, techniques and approaches', and negotiate procedural modifications in collaboration with users and colleagues. The current method is iterative and expert-driven, grounded in reaction to subject area changes or user requests.

Future GSBPM expectation: With automation and interoperability prioritized, the initial identification of concepts shifts to system-guided exercises leveraging AI and metadata. The EC-04’s input is needed for validating, contextualizing, or justifying deviations from enterprise standard concepts, often in compressed timelines and collaborative, cross-program contexts.

Role evolution: The EC-04’s decision-making shifts from conceptual authorship towards arbitration, solution vetting, and the alignment of program content with enterprise frameworks. The officer will lead or participate in review teams working with automated discovery tools, and engage more rigorously in cross-domain prioritization and conflict resolution to ensure enterprise-wide reusability and compliance.

Capability implication: Increased emphasis falls on architectural understanding of statistical concepts, enterprise-level negotiation, identifying when and how to adjust automated suggestions, and awareness of the digital frameworks and metadata repositories that drive automation and harmonization at scale.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: EC-05 positions investigate client requirements, define study scope, modify or create approaches to address unique needs, and review/approve processing parameters, including 'develops data bases for the provision of time-series information', 'interprets preliminary results', and 'reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs.' Translating data with differing definitions into common concepts is a substantial part of the role.

Future GSBPM expectation: The increased use of digital inventories, automated mapping tools, and rigorous adherence to interoperable, reusable statistical assets modifies how new data needs are met. Rather than manually reconciling new requirements, the EC-05 will review and justify choices in the context of established frameworks, participate in rapid arbitration across program boundaries, and help adapt or escalate needs that diverge from available assets.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will now need to focus on the evaluation, arbitration, and contextual justification where automated or system-suggested concepts do not align with program needs. Operational workflows become more consultative, cross-functional, and driven by alignment pressure, rather than bespoke solution creation for each request.

Capability implication: A deeper grasp of metadata-driven systems, interoperability challenges, and the principles of justification/exception handling in a digital asset environment becomes necessary to fulfill this evolved responsibility.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Head, Production and Dissemination
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 oversees the development and implementation of divisional statistical programs, establishes concepts and definitions, manages the integration of multi-source data, and is responsible for resolving compatibility issues and developing policies and guidelines. The position also regularly assesses the need for modification or adaptation of conceptual frameworks across programs, often building ground-up justifications based on program or user-driven requirements.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state expects EC-06 leaders to champion the adoption of automated, metadata-based concept identification systems, ensure divisional alignment with enterprise data assets and FAIR principles, and arbitrate prioritization and exception cases at a cross-divisional or enterprise level. Leaders are accountable for steering the transition from manual to system-curated conceptual frameworks and ensuring scalable, reusable outputs for digital integration.

Role evolution: The EC-06 role evolves from managing isolated program-level conceptual frameworks to leading multi-domain harmonization, setting policies that guide the arbitration of AI-suggested concepts, and driving the adoption of enterprise metadata practices. Leadership responsibilities now encompass orchestrating rapid arbitration processes, justifying deviations from standardized concepts, and integrating outputs with end-to-end automation.

Capability implication: This creates greater reliance on knowledge of enterprise architecture, metadata management, digital governance (e.g., FAIR principles), and the ability to facilitate organizational change toward systemic, automated workflows for concept identification.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Head, Production and Dissemination
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination is responsible for preparing program proposals on statistical frameworks, developing policies, procedures, and guidelines for system development, and determining the methods and practices for data acquisition, production, and dissemination. The role entails evaluating the suitability of new and emerging data sources, reviewing conceptual frameworks, integrating data from a variety of sources (e.g., financial statements, tax files, administrative sources, surveys), and ensuring legislative requirements (including confidentiality, privacy, and data access) are met. The work description emphasizes 'assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and ... identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software and to determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.'

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state outlines a shift to automated, AI-enabled assessments for data availability and suitability, emphasizing a standard, technology-driven prioritization of existing internal and alternative data holdings before considering new surveys. Human expertise is redirected to overseeing automation, resolving complex legal and risk cases, and managing data partnerships. There is a new expectation for transparent, evidence-based justification for survey proposals, in-depth legal/ethical vetting related to third-party or alternative data, and ongoing curation of metadata used for automated discovery.

Role evolution: This role will move from overseeing manual and reactive reviews of data availability to designing and governing processes for automated, systematized, and metadata-driven discovery and assessment of data sources. Decision-making will intensify around legal, ethical, and quality oversight for automated systems, and strategic management of partner relationships and access negotiations (especially with non-traditional and private data holders). The EC-06 will set policies for the use of AI-powered assessment tools, lead in evolving frameworks for data suitability, and arbitrate complex suitability, confidentiality, and legislative edge cases flagged by automation.

Capability implication: Deep contextual and operational knowledge will remain critical but now must extend to evaluating and overseeing AI-driven data discovery, machine-actionable metadata infrastructure, privacy-by-design workflow automation, and risk/impact assessment frameworks. Understanding of dynamic legal and contractual obligations for externally-held data, along with capability in change management for process modernization and partnership negotiation, becomes much more important in the future operating model.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is charged with investigating client requirements, determining data sources for special requests, defining methodologies for retrieving, integrating, and producing statistical information, and negotiating with internal and external stakeholders (including data suppliers). The work description emphasizes working with data from diverse, sometimes non-traditional sources, and adapting methods where data was collected for other purposes using different definitions ('Often, the data have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.'). It also refers to responsibility for establishing and negotiating contracts for projects and discussing data reporting agreements with suppliers.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, initial data source discovery and suitability is automated and prioritized via intelligent, AI-driven systems. The line between internal, administrative, and third-party data sources is blurred, with human experts called in mainly to evaluate complex suitability cases, legal or confidentiality challenges, or to negotiate and manage relationships with new and non-traditional data owners. Proposals for new surveys require strong, system-generated evidence of necessity, and contract/agreement negotiation becomes more pronounced.

Role evolution: The EC-05 specialist's activities shift from primarily manual identification and ad-hoc assessment of potential data sources to curating, interpreting, and resolving suitability and integration issues flagged by automated tools. The role will increasingly focus on interpreting nuanced gaps or challenges not resolved by technology, and leading negotiations or crafting agreements with alternative data suppliers. Their consultative expertise will be leveraged to support evidence-based justifications for any new data collection and to secure access rights consistent with legal and ethical standards for complex sources.

Capability implication: The ability to comprehend and evaluate the output and logic of automated suitability and discovery systems, as well as to provide authoritative input to legal/ethical risk analyses and data access negotiations, is now essential. Detailed understanding of interoperability challenges, metadata structures, and evolving privacy/contractual frameworks will underpin the specialist's consultative authority in the redefined workflow.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 Development Officer develops and maintains processing systems that manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data. The role includes analyzing and proposing modifications to data retrieval systems, conducting feasibility studies regarding new product requirements and data sources, and negotiating procedural modifications with partners based on operational needs. The description highlights 'assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' It also includes evaluating existing and potential subject-matter conflicts, duplication, and data gaps.

Future GSBPM expectation: Automated systems will form the backbone of data discovery, selection, and suitability screening. The threshold for system modification now originates from standardized, exhaustive metadata-driven queries rather than purely program-driven needs. The officer will be less involved in manual data canvassing, but must ensure that automated and AI-assisted workflows are accurately capturing relevant changes, managing data suitability rules, and supporting legal and privacy vetting processes for non-traditional data sources. 

Role evolution: This role becomes more about operationalizing the machine-actionable and automated GSBPM processes, configuring and maintaining the metadata catalogs and suitability screening rules, and translating changing program needs into well-specified development requirements for automated platforms. The EC-04 will also need to validate, troubleshoot, and optimize these automated workflows and manage new types of procedural adaptations stemming from alternative and administrative data landscapes. Their decision input may become more about orchestrating sophisticated, system-embedded workflows than about manual source evaluation.

Capability implication: The role requires deeper conceptual understanding of metadata architecture, suitability rule logic, workflow automation, and privacy/compliance risk triggers within technology-driven frameworks. They will need to anticipate and address the limitations or edge cases of automated suitability screening, collaborating closely with subject-matter, legal, and IT experts in this modernized environment.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator' is responsible for coordinating and organizing dissemination of data, providing advice on data products, and implementing changes to systems used for editing and validation. The work includes 'identifying and evaluating problems related to the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information' and 'determining the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to retrieve, edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data.' This encompasses both procedural and technical aspects of output design and release, currently oriented toward traditional, static, and human-readable products.
Future GSBPM expectation: The future state requires outputs to be 'machine-actionable, standardized, interoperable, and ready for both human and automated consumption by default.' Output design shifts to metadata-driven, programmatically accessible products (e.g., via APIs), emphasizing automation, modularity, and integration with larger dissemination platforms, rather than manual, ad-hoc file creation. Confidentiality, traceability, and ethics are foundational, and staff must collaborate more deeply with IT and metadata specialists.
Role evolution: The Coordinator's activities would shift from organizing and crafting bespoke releases toward specifying, testing, and maintaining standardized dissemination schemas and output protocols within automated or API-driven platforms. The role would require greater engagement in system specification, protocol adoption, automation testing, and documentation for both technical (machine) and human users. Solutions would be less about file preparation and more about ongoing platform and metadata schema development and user enablement.
Capability implication: There is a growing expectation for fluency in data and metadata modeling, understanding principles of machine-actionable and interoperable outputs, and the ability to collaborate with IT/platform leads. Knowledge of open data standards, API-based dissemination, and principles such as FAIR become critical. Understanding and integration of confidentiality, access, and automation compliance must also become core to the role.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' develops processing systems and applications for manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data and leads teams implementing new or modified processing systems. The role involves diagnosing and addressing problems in data dissemination and implementing enhancements to systems, with some focus on 'designing specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases' and 'liaising with subject specialists to translate requirements into system development.'
Future GSBPM expectation: The future state places data dissemination at the core of the statistical production process, requiring outputs to be interoperable, machine-actionable, accessible through APIs, and described by rich, standardized metadata. Dissemination systems must support automation, modularity, embargoed/conditional access, and extensibility for new user requirements. Design and development are no longer about static products but about resilient, scalable, metadata-rich dissemination infrastructures.
Role evolution: The Officer must pivot from customizing processing systems for static file outputs to developing and maintaining frameworks that programmatically generate, manage, and expose outputs to both human and machine users. The role increasingly prioritizes schema and protocol design for interoperability, metadata schemas, scalable access controls, and collaboration with IT/metadata teams to ensure end-to-end automation and compliance. The Officer will be expected to specify, test, and adjust dissemination components as part of broader pipelines, not as bespoke solutions.
Capability implication: A significantly deeper understanding is required of interoperability standards, metadata-driven design, API architectures, and automated workflow integration. Proficiency in confidentiality implementation, access control rules, and protocols for automated and modular data dissemination becomes crucial. Conceptual and practical knowledge of trusted dissemination practices, automation opportunities, and technical specifications for machine-readability are now central to the role.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Specialist develops databases and data systems for both internal and user-facing information delivery, guides teams involved in data manipulation and dissemination, and provides expert advice to stakeholders. Responsibilities include 'develop[ing] guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications,' 'reviewing and approving processing parameters,' and 'ensuring compatibility with other statistical programs.' The role has significant influence on the design, consistency, and standards of data outputs and dissemination procedures, particularly within current, file- and report-based ecosystems.
Future GSBPM expectation: The transformation under StatCan2030 integrates output/dissemination design into core production, necessitating outputs to be machine/actionable, API-accessible, platform-independent, and extensible by default. The focus moves from standardized human-facing products to reusable, automated, and programmatically accessible assets supporting diverse user and agent requirements, including embargo management and advanced metadata linkage.
Role evolution: The Specialist would need to evolve from overseeing static database/report development to designing and implementing output schemas and dissemination frameworks that enable automated, modular data publishing, robust metadata capture, machine-actionability, and layered access rules. Strategic planning would require anticipating reusability, interoperability, and extensibility from the outset, not as an afterthought. Engagement with IT architects, metadata/governance leads, and data privacy/ethics experts increases, reflecting product/platform stewardship rather than ad hoc output fulfillment.
Capability implication: Priority shifts to understanding and applying metadata standards (e.g., for discoverability and interoperability), machine-actionable output principles, automation best practices, and managed disclosure/confidentiality protocols. Platform thinking, systems integration, and the ability to design for programmatic user scenarios become integral, as does the anticipation of future-proofing assets for new consumer types (e.g., AI agents).

implicated work-descriptions.title: Head, Production and Dissemination
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head plans and implements long-term strategies for development, enhancement, and operation of statistical programs, certifies output quality, establishes policies/procedures for dissemination and confidentiality, and oversees conceptual frameworks and integration with external programs. The role's mandate specifically references reviewing and recommending applications of new technologies and methods in mass data processing, but presently this is largely oriented around traditional or semi-automated legacy systems and output modalities.
Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 redefines dissemination as foundational to the entire statistical system, with outputs needing to be automated, metadata- and API-driven, interoperable, discoverable, and available for both human and machine consumption. This strategic shift requires senior program leads to drive not only compliance with such standards, but also systemic transformation—embedding machine-actionable thinking and modularity into design, ensuring robust confidentiality and access rules, and guaranteeing alignment with broader organizational IT and metadata architectures.
Role evolution: The Head must move from overseeing programs which produce human-focused outputs and upgrades, to managing the transition to and operation of standardized, automated dissemination pipelines, including specification, procurement, and evaluation of interoperable platforms. Leadership responsibilities expand to include stewardship of data discoverability, API access, and secure, traceable platforms enabling both human and automated usage. The Head is increasingly accountable for ensuring that the unit delivers not just statistical products, but also trusted, reusable, and extensible dissemination services as a product/platform owner.
Capability implication: This creates a need for in-depth understanding of machine-actionable design, API and automation strategy, advanced metadata architecture, and trust-by-design/ethical release practices at scale. Broader literacy in interoperability frameworks, platform/product management, and the integration of confidentiality/data ethics into technical design becomes imperative. The Head becomes central to driving a product-oriented, scalable approach to data dissemination and leading workforce transformation to support this model.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the retrieval, editing, validation and dissemination of data, and for advising users on subject-matter concepts. The role involves recommending improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implementing changes to processing systems, including the modification or development of statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or meet new needs. Evidence: 'Develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques', 'Provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts', and 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods'.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, variable design will move from project-specific and manual practices toward being a machine-actionable, metadata-rich, and standardized process, aligned with enterprise frameworks and FAIR principles. The role of analysts and methodologists will pivot toward stewarding reusable variable and metadata libraries (rather than one-off variable definitions), ensuring conformance to interoperability standards, and curating the metadata that enables automated production.

Role evolution: The Coordinator’s responsibility for subject-matter concepts and modifications to processing systems will become less about designing variables for one project and more about ensuring adherence to standardized models, describing variables for machine and cross-domain use, and collaborating in enterprise variable stewardship. The work will focus on the integration of variable specifications with central registries, development of rich metadata, and ensuring compatibility for automated pipelines and AI consumption. Decision-making will increasingly involve evaluating the appropriateness of a variable within enterprise standards, versioning and solidifying metadata, and contributing to the governance of variable repositories—often through collaborative, cross-divisional processes.

Capability implication: This requires deeper understanding of metadata frameworks, semantic and interoperability standards, and the operational requirements for automated systems. Knowledge of enterprise-wide variable design, data governance, and the use of collaborative registries and APIs becomes central, as well as the impact of variable choices on automation and cross-domain analytics.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The Development Officer develops and modifies processing systems for storing and retrieving data, develops subject-matter concepts and definitions, and leads teams to improve survey methods and develop new or modified statistical methods, concepts, and approaches. Evidence: 'Develops subject matter concepts and definitions', 'Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems', and 'Identifies and evaluates problems in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical information'.

Future GSBPM expectation: The shift to enterprise-wide, machine-actionable variable standards will require that systems and applications are designed to register, describe, and manage variables in alignment with centralized, standardized frameworks. The Officer will need to ensure that developed systems can support dynamic metadata enrichment, automated variable registries, and seamless interoperability for downstream applications.

Role evolution: The Officer will move from customizing system components for each project to embedding enterprise metadata and standardization at the core of development activities. They will become responsible for designing and supporting systems that enable the registration, stewardship, and API-powered reuse of variables, and for ensuring systems are interoperable and maintainable as new, cross-domain requirements emerge. Collaboration with other domain experts on building or modifying standardized repositories will also become more significant.

Capability implication: This creates heightened demands for knowledge of machine-actionable metadata standards, integration of semantic registries with processing systems, and operationalization of FAIR principles. The ability to evaluate variable stewardship approaches across domains and supervise design or modifications within governance frameworks is now essential.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The Specialist develops databases and coordinates teams manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, providing subject-matter expertise, leading system development activities, and resolving complex issues related to data integration and conceptual conflicts. Evidence: 'Develops databases ... as well as data for special studies and requests', 'reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies', and 'reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs'.

Future GSBPM expectation: Moving toward standardized, metadata-rich variable design, the Specialist's role extends to overseeing the governance and implementation of enterprise-wide variables, supporting automated, ‘AI-ready’ data structures, and leading the integration of domain standards within and across programs. The role no longer focuses on creating bespoke variables, but on maintaining, curating, and improving reusable, richly described variable libraries and systems.

Role evolution: The Specialist will become accountable for ensuring that variable choices at the design and implementation stages conform to enterprise interoperability standards, overseeing the metadata management for both in-house and repurposed external variables, and leading the integration with centralized repositories. The role pivots from managing unique project-based requirements toward managing the lifecycle and quality of shared standards, supporting end-to-end automation and facilitating data integration at scale.

Capability implication: This reinforces the need for robust knowledge of metadata and variable management frameworks, semantic harmonization, repository interoperability, and the methodologies for supporting programmatic and automated integration of data assets. Understanding how choices in variable management affect automation, analytics, and governance becomes critical.

Evidence: 'Plans and implements long term strategies', 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes', and 'Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption.'

Future GSBPM expectation: At future-state, variable design is strategic and foundational, requiring active leadership in establishing and maintaining enterprise-wide, machine-actionable variable and metadata standards. Heads will need to ensure all divisional programs and systems adhere to centralized frameworks, that governance and stewardship of variable assets are robust, and that their area is future-proofed for automation and AI readiness.

Role evolution: The Head’s responsibility for setting frameworks, policies, and standards now encompasses leading the adoption of metadata-rich, interoperability-first cultures and ensuring that system and program designs enable seamless registration, versioning, and reuse of variables across the enterprise. They will be called upon to champion the operational shift, mediate requirements with emerging standards, and drive the division’s engagement in cross-program governance. Decision-making extends to the prioritization and resourcing of metadata stewardship and the integration of new tools and processes that embody FAIR principles.

Capability implication: This intensifies the need for advanced knowledge in enterprise metadata governance, semantic interoperability, the organizational impacts of automation, and strategic change management in statistico-technical environments. Familiarity with the operational, strategic, and technological aspects of enterprise-wide variable standardization and stewardship is essential.

Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer has a central role in designing and implementing statistical processing systems and in conducting feasibility studies regarding new system and product requirements, as described by statements such as 'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program.' The position also 'proposes new statistical methods, techniques and approaches or the modification of existing techniques and approaches to improve program coverage or to meet specific needs.'

Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 transforms 'Design collection' to prioritize alternative and administrative data sources, mandates automated and modular tools, and employs AI for instrument generation, minimizing manual, bespoke survey creation. EC-04s previously engaged in instrument-by-instrument design and manual specification would now be expected to leverage AI-driven, reusable platforms and ensure their outputs meet interoperability, discoverability, and transparency requirements.

Role evolution: The role shifts from direct design and customization of collection systems for each program to building and maintaining robust frameworks, configuring modular components, validating AI outputs, and overseeing the ethical and technical compliance of automated solutions. Project work moves from bespoke, iterative tool-building to enabling and monitoring standardized, scalable platforms and question banks accessible organization-wide. Coordination with IT and metadata specialists becomes routine, as does acting as a subject-matter validator or supervisor of automated processes, rather than sole author of collection instruments.

Capability implication: This implies a greater need for fluency in metadata-driven collection infrastructure, platform and API conceptualization, and oversight of machine-generated survey content. It demands new depth in evaluating system-level impacts, configuring and monitoring automation, and a foundational understanding of interoperability, data integration strategies, and the ethical, audit, and governance requirements associated with AI-driven tools.

The emphasis moves from solving individual project collection needs to systematizing and monitoring collection logic and platform effectiveness across subject-matter domains.

Role evolution: The work moves from hands-on creation and troubleshooting of data collection tools and systems to higher-level stewardship of framework configuration, curation of standardized question banks or data integration points, and exception handling in automated, AI-driven processes. The role will also require greater involvement in cross-functional initiatives to align subject-matter frameworks with interoperable and machine-actionable standards, acting as a bridge between content experts, IT and metadata architects, and AI automation supervisors. Leadership and decision-making shifts from tactical to strategic, with emphasis on monitoring, governance, and adaptability across multiple, reusable systems.

Capability implication: The position will need deeper familiarity with metadata frameworks, automated workflow oversight, enterprise architecture concepts, real-time validation of AI-driven outputs, and the co-creation of ethical, standardized collection methodologies. The role becomes more about steering evolving technologies and platforms to sustain quality and relevancy than about direct instrument-by-instrument design.

EC-06s will oversee the transition from labor-intensive survey design to validating and improving AI-based, data-source-first pipelines, and ensuring their units comply with updated transparency, audit, and ethical oversight mandates, while maintaining efficiency and quality.

Role evolution: Rather than guiding incremental improvements in legacy program designs, EC-06s must architect and enforce adoption of modular, standardized systems, facilitate cross-divisional integration of collection frameworks, and implement enterprise-wide monitoring, auditability, and exception management processes for AI automation in the design collection phase. Responsibility expands to include oversight of AI model validation, configuration of guardrails for automation, and ensuring systems-level interoperability. Their authority and accountability extend beyond their unit to the broader operational ecosystem, with heightened stakes for compliance, scalability, and real-time responsiveness.

Capability implication: They will need advanced knowledge of modular system architecture, AI automation governance, metadata management, and cross-system interoperability. Expertise in leading organizational change, implementing audit trails for automated decisions, and upholding ethical and transparency requirements in a highly automated environment becomes essential.

Key activities include developing specifications, leading implementation of new statistical systems, and integrating subject-matter concepts into system development. Future GSBPM expectation: In the future-state, sampling frame and sample design become largely embodied within automated, metadata-driven, and interoperable systems, requiring integration with AI modules and logic engines that dynamically determine when and how to construct samples versus relying on alternative data. Role evolution: The officer will move from developing and modifying manual/semiautomated frame/sample systems to overseeing, specifying, and validating automated, AI-assisted pipelines for sampling, focusing on configuring metadata, ensuring system logic meets subject-matter requirements, and handling exceptional cases outside routine automation. Notably, they are described as reviewing integration of data 'from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses),' and devising 'criteria and methods' for data consistency and compatibility, which encompasses legacy, manually designed frame and sample construction. Future GSBPM expectation: The transformation to automation shifts the role toward interpreting and approving automatically generated frame/sample designs, guiding how administrative or alternative data are pulled into modular systems, and resolving ambiguous sampling problems flagged by AI or automated systems. Role evolution: This specialist will direct less manual design work and more oversight of automated systems, validate AI-generated sample/frame choices for appropriateness, and ensure standards compliance, focusing on exception handling, systemic improvement of automation, and high-level system integration. Capability implication: Deep knowledge of automated statistical infrastructure becomes critical along with the ability to interpret and defend automated frame/sample selections, assure quality control with cross-domain interoperability, and understand the implications of integrating both legacy and new data sources into sampling automation.

They are responsible for 'determining the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied' and 'reviewing the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs,' including those that determine how populations are framed and samples are drawn. Future GSBPM expectation: The shift to fully automated, AI-orchestrated sampling pipelines demands that program heads define strategy and policies for the integration of AI-enabled selection, establish oversight mechanisms for systemized, modular, interoperable process automation, and handle division-wide exceptions, ethical considerations, and quality assurance in an environment where surveys are a last—rather than default—resort. Role evolution: The Head's task will change from guiding improvements to manual systems and setting traditional methodological policies to setting parameters for automated logic, overseeing system performance and ethical/quality implications of AI-driven sampling, and resolving high-impact exceptions or failures in automated selection. Capability implication: This requires advanced capability in understanding the intersection of statistical methodology, automated system design, AI, and governance/ethics frameworks for automation, as well as the ability to guide staff in integrating alternative data into operational sampling logic and ensure compliance with national and international metadata and interoperability standards.

Coordinators must be adept not only with subject matter and statistical concepts but also with how those are expressed, validated, versioned, and audited in modernized, automated, and metadata-centric systems.

title: GSBPM 5.3 Review and Validate – Future-State Implications

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 role is directly involved in the coordination, organization, and execution of data retrieval, editing, and especially validation. The work description specifically references the need to "design specifications for the editing and validation of data" and to "recommend improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data." Manual data validation and subject-matter-driven review are core parts of the position’s remit.

Future GSBPM expectation: The transformation of review and validate from manual, survey-centric checks to embedded, automated, and auditable rule-driven processes shifts the focus away from hands-on inspection toward managing, configuring, and improving validation logic, as well as monitoring outputs and exception cases flagged by automation.

Role evolution: This role must migrate from conducting and coordinating routine manual validation to focusing on the design and specification of validation modules that can be automated, implementing and evaluating their performance, and supporting the development of transparent, standardized logic that is reusable and auditable. Analysts will be expected to monitor automated systems, manage exceptions, and proactively analyze validation outcomes, rather than perform manual checking.

Capability implication: Increased emphasis will be on understanding and formalizing validation logic, using automation/orchestration tools, assessing AI-enabled validation results, and working with auditable, version-controlled processes. Subject-matter knowledge will need to be codified for transfer to automated systems, and analysts must be able to interpret and improve the logic and algorithms driving validation modules.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 position has explicit duties developing processing systems, designing specifications for data testing, and leading operational improvements. This includes the "development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems" and the "design specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases." The position is also charged with addressing problems in statistical data manipulation and providing solutions or recommendations relating to validation.

Future GSBPM expectation: Automated and AI-enabled validation, embedded within pipelines, will dominate future workloads. EC-04s are expected to replace point-in-time, manual validation or custom code with standardized, reusable, modular validation functions that operate transparently across different domains and sources.

Role evolution: The role must pivot toward engineering robust, automated, and metadata-driven validation tools, ensuring standardization, portability, and auditability of validation logic, and integrating these modules within orchestrated pipelines. The focus will also include continuous improvement, exception management, and possibly tuning of AI/ML models for validation tasks.

Capability implication: Deep understanding of automatable validation logic and process orchestration becomes crucial, along with advanced familiarity with pipeline tools, reproducibility practices, and automation. Abstraction and translation of subject-matter rules to programmable formats, plus evaluation of AI performance and exception outcomes, become central activities.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Specialist leads or coordinates units involved in manipulating, storing, and especially "retrieving" validated data, developing guidelines for system evaluation and testing, and recommends improvements to existing validation procedures. The role includes "reviews and approves detailed processing parameters," "develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems," and "reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs," all of which are closely aligned with the review and validation stage.

Future GSBPM expectation: Specialists must guide and ensure the operationalization of automated, scalable, and standardized validation practices, limiting manual interventions to edge-case analysis and quality oversight.

Role evolution: This position will transition from direct review of data and ad hoc process improvements to governance, monitoring, and continuous quality assurance of validation modules and their outputs, as well as oversight of validation exception management and root-cause analysis. EC-05s are likely to lead efforts in adapting subject-matter-driven validation requirements into standard automated rules and monitor validation pipelines for both performance and integrity.

Capability implication: The capacity to “translate” complex subject-matter logic into programmable and auditable rules, lead cross-domain standardization, scrutinize automated validation outcomes, and ensure audit trails will be critical. Understanding process automation, version control of logic, and hybrid governance (AI/human) processes will take on greater importance.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Head, Production and Dissemination
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 role is responsible for long-term planning and implementation of statistical programs, development and operation of systems, review and certification of data quality, and the establishment of "policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for development, use and evaluation of systems and processes," including those for validation. The head also “reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results” and "establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems, equipment, databases and files."

Future GSBPM expectation: With validation as a transparent, automated, and auditable pipeline step, operational and strategic oversight will center on ensuring automation performs to rigorous, standardized, and reproducible quality standards, and on cross-program/enterprise harmonization of validation modules.

Role evolution: The Head’s leadership, oversight, and resource planning must prioritize the transition to automated, AI-enabled validation systems, driving efforts to embed and govern these modules across domains. The position’s accountability pivots from judging manual/case-by-case validation methods to developing frameworks for pipeline monitoring, module certification, governance of exception management, and continual validation logic refinement.

Capability implication: A sophisticated understanding of automated validation design, operational governance of AI-enabled logic, and assurance of auditability and process resilience are now foundational. Ensuring that validation processes are standardized across programs and defensible to both internal and external auditors will be core to the role.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator' is directly responsible for coordinating, organizing, and in many cases, conducting the retrieval, editing, validation, and dissemination of statistical data. This includes designing specifications for editing/validation, resolving technical and subject-matter problems related to data quality, and making recommendations for improvements to processing systems. Evidence includes statements such as 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation ... of data', 'Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures', and 'Develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys.'
Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, editing and imputation are executed predominantly by AI-driven, highly automated, and modular pipelines, reducing manual, program-specific interventions. Analysts are expected to oversee algorithm performance, handle rare exceptions, and continuously validate system outputs for reproducibility and explainability, instead of hands-on correction. All edit/impute decisions must be transparent, auditable, and standardized, shifting the main responsibility from individual judgment towards governance of automated systems.
Role evolution: The EC-03 will thus shift from hands-on editing, rule implementation, and direct intervention to configuring, monitoring, and overseeing automated processes. The role will require active participation in the validation, auditing, and improvement of edit/impute algorithms and pipelines, focusing less on user-driven data cleaning and more on continuous system assurance, exception resolution, and cross-program standardization. Decision-making will involve diagnosing system-level and algorithmic errors, setting parameters, and interpreting automated results within governance frameworks rather than manual data handling.
Capability implication: This transformation will require a deeper understanding of pipeline configuration, AI model logic and their error/fairness points, automation audit trails, and system troubleshooting for exception cases. Knowledge of data governance and regulatory standards grows in importance, as does the ability to interpret the impact of algorithmic editing or imputation decisions and communicate them to stakeholders and clients (internally and externally).

implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' is tasked with developing and maintaining processing systems and applications for data manipulation, including designing, testing, and modifying the systems that underpin editing and imputation operations. Key responsibilities cite 'Develops processing systems ... to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data' and 'Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications.' The role also acts as a subject matter advisor and leads system-related teams and projects.
Future GSBPM expectation: With massive advances in automation, this role must move from incremental improvement and custom solutioning towards enabling and orchestrating integrated, AI-oriented edit/impute microservices. EC-04s are expected to support automated, standardized, and auditable pipelines—and thus must drive the deployment, auditing, and exception management of these new operational frameworks, prioritizing cross-program consistency and reuse over program-specific tailoring. Their work becomes one of oversight of modular workflow orchestration, not direct solution design for every edit case.
Role evolution: The EC-04 role will need to transition from strong solution design and coding for individual programs’ needs to a focus on configuring, integrating, overseeing, and evolving enterprise-level automated pipelines. New responsibilities will include testing and evaluation of edit/impute automation components, troubleshooting algorithmic outputs, and adapting modular pipelines for varying program requirements, while ensuring reproducibility and governance. Less time is spent on writing or maintaining legacy scripts; more is spent on validation, explainability, and alignment with agency-wide architectural standards.
Capability implication: EC-04s must become proficient in orchestrated workflow platforms, the workings and evaluation of AI-powered components, the principles of auditable automation, and the regulatory or ethical considerations of algorithmic decision-making. A thorough understanding of automation framework design, as well as risk/exception escalation processes, gains in importance as the bridge between subject-matter knowledge and advanced technical environments.

implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated work-descriptions.justification:
